toc.text: The Product2 object: what you actually sell
Price books and price book entries

html:
Before a single discount or approval rule can run, the configurator needs something to configure. The product catalog answers three questions: what can we sell (Product2), for how much and in which currency (Pricebook2 / PricebookEntry), and in what combinations (features, options, bundles, product rules). This is Phase 02 of the Academy, and it is deliberately the phase every implementation builds first — pricing, quoting, and contracting all hang off the catalog.

In this guide you will model a real catalog: products with families, categories, standard and custom price books, features and options that make a product configurable, bundle parents that roll up options, and the native Revenue Cloud catalog objects (ProductCatalog, ProductSellingModel) that the next-generation engine uses.

Learning objectives

  • Model a sellable item on Product2 and explain the difference between a product and a product variant.
  • Relate price books to product families using Pricebook2 and PricebookEntry and explain the standard price book's role.
  • Outline how product families drive both reporting and discount logic (Product_Family__c in discount schedules).
  • Describe features, options, and constraints and how they turn a flat SKU into a configurable product.
  • Explain the bundle relationship: one parent line with zero or more option lines.
  • Distinguish the classic CPQ SBQQ__ configuration hierarchy from the Revenue Cloud catalog (ProductCatalog, ProductSellingModel).
  • Query the catalog with SOQL and see it flow into real quote lines.
  • Apply catalog hygiene rules (activation, naming, currency, inactive cleanup).
  • Prepare the catalog layer that phases 03–05 will build on.

The Product2 object: what you actually sell

Product2 is the stock-keeping record. The fields that matter most to a CPQ implementation are:

FieldPurposePractical advice
NameDisplay nameKeep it human; it shows on quotes and documents
FamilyCoarse grouping (picklist)Drives reporting and their own discount schedules
IsActiveSoft deletionInactive products cannot be quoted
ProductCodeExternal SKUMap 1:1 with your ERP / catalog source
DescriptionLong textFeeds quote descriptions and contract language
QuantityUnitOfMeasureSeats, licenses, GBNeeded for subscription-style catalogs

Families are the catalog's primary dimension. In this project every Discount_Schedule__c carries a Product_Family__c, so a "software" family and a "services" family can price very differently in later phases.

Price books and price book entries

A product has many possible prices; a price book entry pins one price to one product inside one price book. The chain is:

text
Product2 (what) ── PricebookEntry (how much) ── Pricebook2 (which book/currency)

The standard price book is auto-created by Salesforce and the price an org usually sells at. A custom price book allows a different price for a channel (partner, region, promo) while the product stays the same.

ConceptObjectCardinalityExample
ProductProduct21 product"Revenue Cloud Core"
EntryPricebookEntryN entries per productUSD 1000 / month, EUR 950 / month
BookPricebook21..N booksStandard, EMEA Partner, EDU

Only active entries with the standard price book as their basis can be quoted, and a quote is always bound to one Pricebook2Id. This is why the classic "no matching price book entry" error appears the moment someone inserts a QuoteLineItem under a mismatched book.

soql
SELECT Product2Id, Product2.Name, Product2.Family, UnitPrice, IsActive, CurrencyIsoCode
FROM PricebookEntry
WHERE Pricebook2.IsStandard = true AND IsActive = true
ORDER BY Product2.Family, Product2.Name
Tip — Keep the standard price book as the single source of list truth and let custom books express discounts off it. Importing the same product at two different absolute prices hides the discount lineage and ruins leakage reporting.

Product families and catalog grouping

Families are the category axis of the catalog and the cheapest analytics you will ever build. Typical families for a subscription business: Software, Cloud Consumption, Support, Professional Services, Hardware.

Families matter beyond cosmetics:

  • Reporting — every revenue report can pivot on Product2.Family.
  • Pricing rules — PriceRuleEngineService.resolveDiscountPercent(productFamily, amount) matches discount schedules by family first, then dollar amount.
  • Approvals & margins — finance approves different discount ceilings per family.

For consistency, the Academy dataset uses family names in the Discount_Schedule__c.Product_Family__c field, so a schedule with Product_Family__c = 'Software' only prices software lines, and a schedule with a blank family acts as a global fallback.

Features, options, and configuration

A feature is a product attribute a buyer can change; an option is one possible value of that feature. A laptop: CPU (feature) → i5, i7, i9 (options). The set of selected options is the configuration.

In the classic CPQ model this lives on SBQQ__ProductFeature__c and SBQQ__Option__c. Because this Academy runs on standard + custom objects, configuration is represented on the quote line itself:

QuoteLineItem fieldUsed to model
Is_Bundle_Parent__cThe product is the "shell" of a bundle
Bundle_Option__cThe selected option value, named as Group: Option (e.g. Storage: 100 GB)

Two lines with Storage: 100 GB and Storage: 500 GB on the same bundle are a conflict — your BundleConfigurationService.hasConflictingOptions catches exactly this shape, just like a single-select option group in CPQ.

Bundles

A bundle is one sellable product that is made of other products. You price the parts, then roll up.

RoleHow the line is flaggedExample
Parent (bundle shell)Is_Bundle_Parent__c = true"Workstation Bundle"
Included featureOption line, included by defaultOS, power cable
Optional featureOption line the buyer selectsi7 CPU, 32 GB RAM
Linked productStandalone lineExtended warranty, year 2

BundleConfigurationService.rollupBundlePrice computes the bundle price as the sum of its selected option lines; when options exist the parent's own price is replaced by the option roll-up so the bundle never double counts.

Configurable products and constraint patterns

Configuration without constraints is chaos. Real CPQ configurators ship four kinds of constraints, and they map onto what this project validates in Apex:

ConstraintReal-world wordingProject equivalent
Required option"A server must have an OS"Validation rule: parent must have ≥ 1 option line
Single-select"Pick one storage tier"hasConflictingOptions on a Group: prefix
Exclusion"i9 only with 32 GB+ RAM"Rule check across option values
Price adjustment"Choosing 500 GB adds +200"Roll-up pricing of the selected option lines

The classic CPQ package expresses these as SBQQ__ProductRule__c records with a Selection, Validation, Price, or Filter rule type. Conceptually identical checks happen in this project inside BundleConfigurationService.validateBundleConfiguration.

The Revenue Cloud catalog (RLM)

The next-generation engine replaces Product2-adjacent configuration with a formal catalog and selling model:

ObjectRole
ProductCatalogThe container of everything sellable (a tree of categories + products)
ProductSellingModelHow a product can be sold: options, dynamic constraints, pricing model
ProductCatalogEntryLinks products into a catalog with attributes
PriceBookEntryStill the pricing anchor — price books were not removed

Where classic CPQ puts configuration on SBQQ__Option__c, RLM puts it on the selling model so the same base product can be sold through different lenses (e.g. on a subscription vs perpetual contract). Two implementations, one mental model: products + rules + price points.

Catalog hygiene

  • Activation discipline — never quote inactive products or entries; they fail with record-not-found errors at line insertion.
  • Naming conventions — parity between Product2.Name and ProductCode avoids ERP reconciliation bugs.
  • One currency model — a multi-currency org needs one entry per product per currency, not a product with a baked-in currency.
  • Retire, don't delete — deactivate and archive instead of deleting products that appear in existing contracts and orders.
  • Families before rules — decide the family list first; it becomes a foreign key into discount schedules and leakage reports.
Tip — A catalog is a published artifact. Treat the change like a release: review product activation, re-run catalog-to-quote integration tests, and only then announce it to the sales team.

Hands-on walkthrough

This walkthrough builds a small catalog with families and options, then pushes it through the quote pipeline using this repo's data model and services.

  1. Create your products with families in Anonymous Apex (or via the UI). Mirror the golden-path test exactly:

    apex
    insert new List<Product2>{
    new Product2(Name = 'Laptop Pro', Family = 'Hardware', ProductCode = 'HW-LP-PRO', IsActive = true),
    new Product2(Name = 'Workstation Bundle', Family = 'Hardware', ProductCode = 'HW-WS-BUNDLE', IsActive = true),
    new Product2(Name = 'Revenue Cloud Core', Family = 'Software', ProductCode = 'SW-RCCORE', IsActive = true),
    new Product2(Name = 'Priority Support', Family = 'Support', ProductCode = 'SV-PRIO', IsActive = true)
};

  2. Add price book entries for the standard price book so every product is quotable:

    apex
    List<Product2> products = [SELECT Id, ProductCode FROM Product2 WHERE IsActive = true];
List<PricebookEntry> entries = new List<PricebookEntry>();
for (Product2 p : products) {
    entries.add(new PricebookEntry(Pricebook2Id = Test.getStandardPricebookId(),
        Product2Id = p.Id, UnitPrice = 1000, IsActive = true));
}
insert entries;

  3. Audit the catalog with SOQL — verify family, price, and activation in one read:

    soql
    SELECT Product2.Family, Product2.Name, UnitPrice, IsActive
FROM PricebookEntry
WHERE Pricebook2.IsStandard = true
ORDER BY Product2.Family

  4. Flow the catalog into a quote. Create the quote and two lines — one plain product, one flagged as a bundle parent — the way later modules will:

    apex
    Id stdPb = [SELECT Id FROM Pricebook2 WHERE IsStandard = true LIMIT 1].Id;
Id oppId = [SELECT Id FROM Opportunity LIMIT 1].Id;
Quote q = new Quote(Name = 'Q-CATALOG', OpportunityId = oppId, Pricebook2Id = stdPb);
insert q;

List<PricebookEntry> entries = [SELECT Id, Product2.ProductCode FROM PricebookEntry
                                WHERE Product2.ProductCode IN ('HW-LP-PRO','SW-RCCORE')];
List<QuoteLineItem> lines = new List<QuoteLineItem>();
for (PricebookEntry pe : entries) {
    lines.add(new QuoteLineItem(QuoteId = q.Id, PricebookEntryId = pe.Id,
        Quantity = 10, UnitPrice = pe.UnitPrice,
        List_Unit_Price__c = pe.UnitPrice, Net_Unit_Price__c = pe.UnitPrice));
}
insert lines;   // nothing hits a "no entry" guard because the book matches

  5. Price it with the service layer and confirm totals on the quote:

    apex
    QuoteCalculatorService.recalculateTotals(new Set<Id>{ q.Id });
Quote check = [SELECT Id, Total_ARR__c, Discount_Percent__c FROM Quote WHERE Id = :q.Id];
System.debug('Catalog quote total: ' + check.Total_ARR__c);

  6. Expand into configuration: add Workstation Bundle as Is_Bundle_Parent__c = true and one option line, then run the bundle validation service (Phase 04 drills into this):

    apex
    List<String> issues = BundleConfigurationService
    .validateBundleConfiguration([SELECT Id, Is_Bundle_Parent__c, Bundle_Option__c FROM QuoteLineItem WHERE QuoteId = :q.Id]);
System.debug(issues); // empty list => valid bundle shape

Common pitfalls

  • Quoting without a price book entry. QuoteLineItem insert fails with a price book error if the entry is inactive or belongs to a different book. Verify Pricebook2Id on quote and entry first.
  • Non-unique family names. Families are grouping strings — a typo ('Software' vs 'software') silently kills discount-schedule matches. Use a picklist to enforce consistency.
  • Products mutated instead of versioned. Editing an existing product changes past quotes' display names. Prefer new versions + deactivation.
  • No activation check in processes. A trigger that quotes from Product2 without filtering IsActive = true will surface weird "not found" bugs at contract time.
  • Confusing bundle roll-up with double counting. rollupBundlePrice replaces the parent price with its option sum; pricing both the parent and the options double counts the bundle.
  • Modeling options inside Product2. A product record is not an option. Keep variants/configurations on the line (Bundle_Option__c) or the selling model so the catalog stays flat and auditable.

Key takeaways

  • Product2 (what) → PricebookEntry (how much) → Pricebook2 (which book) is the spine of every sellable item.
  • Product families are a strategic axis: they drive reporting and are the join key for Discount_Schedule__c.Product_Family__c.
  • Features and options make a product configurable; in this project configuration is captured on quote lines via Is_Bundle_Parent__c and Bundle_Option__c (Group: Option).
  • A bundle is one parent plus option lines; option roll-up produces its price.
  • Constraints (required, single-select, exclusion, price adjustment) are validated by BundleConfigurationService.
  • Revenue Cloud / RLM models the same ideas natively through ProductCatalog, ProductSellingModel, and price books.
  • A clean, active, family-consistent catalog is the precondition for every rule, price, and template that comes after it.
